text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ECONOMISTUL
- The newspaper presents a report on the situation in construction, including railway and roads.
BURSA
- State-run Renel electricity authority wants to re-enter the international capital market with a bonds issue.
- Restructuring of the Romanian National Oil Company was delayed for July 25.
- Bancorex SA said it had signed a syndicated loan worth $75 million with Credit Suisse First Boston.
- The transport ministry will offer shares in the maritime and aviation fleet.
ADEVARUL
- The seven poorest counties from south Romania set up a "southern development region".
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The lower chamber of deputies adopted a bill allowing the government to rule by drecee during parliament's summer holiday.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The Black Sea port of Constanta could become a transit point for the oil from the Caspian Sea, says the newspaper.
- The newspaper publishes bills on sponsorship.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- Companies listed on the Bucharest stock exchange are waiting for brokerage houses to get more involved in dealings, says the newspaper. Listed companies are also eager for the State Ownership Fund to sell its shares.
General:
ADEVARUL
- The National Peasant Party wants to change present laws and return to former owners all properties confiscated by the communist regime.
- Striking coal miners in the western Jiu Valley asked for Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea to return from the United States straight to their workplace.

- A group of "dissidents" in the former ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR), including former Foreign Minister Teodor Melescanu, will present their political programme today, ahead of the PDSR national conference due at the weekend.
- The Bucharest court of appeal refused to release miners' union leader Miron Cosma from detention. Cosma is on trial charged with undermining the state during 1991 miner-led riots.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The newspaper presents how the world's major espionage services are organised and function.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The newspaper publishes letters sent by U.S. President Bill Clinton and France's Jacques Chirac expressing support for Romania in its bid to join NATO.

- Clinton's verdict leaving Romania out of the first group of ex-communist countries to be invited to join NATO is the most harsh punishment administered to the former ruling coalition, said Senator Radu Alexandru of the Democratic Party, member of the current government.
- The Romanian parliament is likely to meet in a special session from June 30, when it should recess to July 10.
-- Bucharest Newsroom, 40-1 3120264
